# Taxonomy of Grid-Based Logic Puzzles

## I. By Primary Task Type

### A. Loop/Path Drawing
Puzzles where the solver draws a single continuous loop or path through the grid.

#### A1. Pure Loop Construction
- **Masyu** – Loop constrained by black/white circle turning rules
- **Slitherlink** – Loop drawn on grid edges constrained by number clues
- **Mid-loop** – Loop where black circles mark midpoints of straight segments
- **Nagareru** – Directional loop with wind constraints
- **Moon-or-Sun** – Loop alternating between moon/sun symbols across rooms
- **Dotchi-Loop** – Loop constrained by white circles (all straight or all turning per region) and avoiding black circles
- **Suraromu** – Loop passing through numbered gates in order, starting/ending at a numbered circle

#### A2. Loop + Cell Shading
- **Yajilin** – Loop drawn while placing black cells indicated by directional number clues

#### A3. Path/Connection Drawing
- **Numberlink** – Connect pairs of identical numbers with non-crossing paths
- **Hashiwokakero** – Connect island nodes with bridges (1 or 2) to form a connected network

---

### B. Cell Shading / Painting
Puzzles where the solver determines which cells to shade black (or leave white).

#### B1. Shading with Number Clues on Grid Cells
- **Nurikabe** – Numbers define white island sizes; black cells form one connected wall with no 2×2
- **Kurodoko** – Numbers count visible white cells in four directions; black cells don't touch, white cells connected
- **Kurotto** – Circle numbers indicate sum of adjacent black cell groups
- **Heyawake** – Numbers in rooms indicate count of shaded cells; adjacency and connectivity constraints
- **Akari** – Place light bulbs that illuminate rows/columns; numbered black cells constrain adjacent bulb count
- **Usowan** – Numbers indicate adjacent shaded cells, but exactly one number per room is wrong

#### B2. Shading with Shape Constraints
- **Choco Banana** – Black regions must be rectangles/squares; white regions must not be rectangles/squares; numbers give area
- **Norinori** – Exactly two shaded cells (forming a domino) per bold-lined region
- **LITS** – Shade exactly one tetromino per region; same-shape tetrominoes can't touch; connected, no 2×2
- **Nurimisaki** – Circle cells are white "promontories" (one white neighbor); no 2×2 of either color; white connected
- **Nuritwin** – Each region has exactly two same-sized shaded blocks; all shading connected; no 2×2
- **Shakashaka** – Place triangles so remaining white areas form rectangles; numbers count adjacent triangles

#### B3. Shading with Gravity/Physical Constraint
- **Sto-stone** – Shade cells in rooms (number gives count); when "dropped" they fill bottom half of grid

#### B4. Shading to Create Maze
- **Nurimeizu** – Paint entire rooms black/white to create a maze from S to G with shortest-path constraints

#### B5. Shading with Tile/Region Constraints
- **Tilepaint** – Color entire tiles; diagonal-cell numbers specify black cell counts in rows/columns
- **Chained Block** – Shade cells to form numbered blocks that chain diagonally; unique shapes per chain

---

### C. Region Division / Partitioning
Puzzles where the solver divides the grid into regions by drawing borders.

#### C1. Division into Specific Shapes
- **Shikaku** – Divide grid into rectangles, each containing exactly one number equal to its area
- **Five Cells** – Divide grid into pentominoes; numbers indicate surrounding block edges
- **Sashigane** – Divide grid into L-shaped blocks; circles mark bends, arrows point toward bends

#### C2. Division with Matching/Symmetry Constraints
- **Double Choco** – Divide into blocks where each block has matching white and gray sub-regions of same shape

---

### D. Number/Symbol Placement
Puzzles where the solver fills cells with numbers or symbols.

#### D1. Latin Square Variants
- **Sudoku** – Place 1–9 in rows, columns, and 3×3 boxes without repetition
- **Hitori** – Remove duplicates from rows/columns by shading; black cells don't touch; white cells connected

#### D2. Region-Based Number Fill
- **Fillomino** – Fill numbers forming polyomino blocks of that size; same-sized blocks can't touch
- **Ripple Effect** – Fill rooms with 1 to N; repeated numbers in a line must have sufficient spacing
- **Makaro** – Fill rooms with 1 to N; arrows in black cells point to the largest adjacent number; no same-number adjacency across rooms
- **Nansuke** – Place digit strings from a given list into a crossword-style grid

#### D3. Number Placement with Movement
- **Hebi** – Place snake segments (1–5) in white cells with visibility and non-adjacency constraints

---

### E. Object Placement / Movement
Puzzles where the solver places or moves specific objects.

#### E1. Placement
- **Akari** (also in B1) – Place light bulbs in white cells
- **Evolomino** – Place growing polyomino blocks along arrow paths

#### E2. Movement
- **Satogaeri** – Move numbered circles within countries so each country has exactly one; tracks can't cross
- **Yosenabe** – Move circles straight into gray areas; arrows can't cross; gray area sums must match

---

### F. Line/Mark Filling
Puzzles where every cell receives a symbol or mark.

- **Juosan** – Fill every cell with — or |; territory numbers constrain the difference; runs limited in perpendicular direction
- **Pencils** – Identify pencil shapes and draw lines from tips through a specified number of cells

---

## II. By Constraint Mechanism

### Connectivity Constraints
All white (or all shaded) cells must form a single connected group:
Nurikabe, Kurodoko, Hitori, Heyawake, LITS, Nurimisaki, Nuritwin, Nurimeizu, Usowan, Hashiwokakero

### No 2×2 Constraints
No 2×2 block of same color allowed:
Nurikabe, LITS, Nurimisaki, Nuritwin, Sto-stone, Nurimeizu

### Adjacency Prohibition (same-color cells can't touch)
Black cells can't be orthogonally adjacent:
Hitori, Kurodoko, Yajilin, Usowan, Heyawake

### Room/Region Constraints
Grid pre-divided into rooms with per-room rules:
Heyawake, Moon-or-Sun, Double Choco, Makaro, Ripple Effect, Norinori, Nuritwin, Nurimeizu, Sto-stone, Usowan, Suraromu, Dotchi-Loop, Tilepaint

### Directional/Arrow Clues
Numbers with directional arrows constrain counts or positions:
Yajilin, Makaro, Hebi, Yosenabe, Nagareru, Sashigane, Pencils

### Visibility/Line-of-Sight Clues
Numbers count cells or objects visible along rows/columns:
Akari, Kurodoko, Nurimisaki

---

## III. By Information Given vs. Derived

### Clues Fixed on Grid (solver adds new content)
Sudoku, Fillomino, Ripple Effect, Makaro, Nansuke, Akari, all shading puzzles, all loop puzzles

### Clues Modified/Moved (solver transforms given content)
Satogaeri, Yosenabe, Hitori (shading over existing numbers)

---

## IV. By Grid Element Type

| Element | Puzzles |
|---|---|
| **Dots/vertices** | Slitherlink |
| **Cell edges** | Five Cells, Shikaku, Sashigane, Double Choco |
| **Cell centers (paths)** | Masyu, Mid-loop, Nagareru, Moon-or-Sun, Dotchi-Loop, Suraromu, Yajilin, Numberlink |
| **Cell interiors (shading)** | Nurikabe, Kurodoko, Kurotto, Heyawake, Norinori, LITS, Choco Banana, Shakashaka, Nurimisaki, Nuritwin, Sto-stone, Tilepaint, Usowan, Akari, Hitori, Chained Block, Nurimeizu |
| **Cell interiors (numbers/symbols)** | Sudoku, Fillomino, Ripple Effect, Makaro, Nansuke, Juosan, Hebi |
| **Inter-node connections** | Hashiwokakero |
| **Objects with movement arrows** | Satogaeri, Yosenabe, Pencils, Evolomino |
